theories.name: Strongly Interacting Massive Particle (SIMP) 3-to-2 relic mechanism
theories.summary: A proposed dark-matter thermal relic whose abundance can be set by dark-sector 3-to-2 number-changing interactions while weaker visible-sector scattering maintains kinetic equilibrium.
theories.core: In the original SIMP scenario, dark 3-to-2 reactions determine chemical freeze-out while interactions with the visible bath remove heat; this differs from ordinary 2-to-2 WIMP freeze-out.

theories.name: Elastically Decoupling Relic (ELDER) dark matter
theories.summary: A proposed cold thermal dark-matter relic whose abundance is mainly fixed by elastic-scattering decoupling from ordinary matter before its dark-sector 3-to-2 reactions freeze out.
theories.core: Visible-sector kinetic decoupling occurs while dark 3-to-2 self-reactions continue, generating a separate cannibal epoch before chemical freeze-out.

formulas.name: SIMP 3-to-2 number-density Boltzmann equation
formulas.plain: dn_chi/dt + 3H n_chi = -(n_chi^3 - n_chi^2 n_chi,eq)<sigma v^2>_3->2 - (n_chi^2 - n_chi,eq^2)<sigma v>_ann
formulas.description: The original single-species SIMP number-density balance with dark 3-to-2 self-annihilation, visible-sector pair annihilation/inverse production, and expansion dilution.
assumptions: Homogeneous expanding background, one effective dark species χ and a thermally averaged reaction network as in Hochberg et al. (2014).
Rapid dark 2-to-2 scattering and effective visible-sector kinetic equilibrium permit a common bath temperature and equilibrium density n_eq.
The 3-to-2 and 2-to-2 processes use the original author's thermal-rate conventions, not a universal reaction network for asymmetric or multiple-species models.
No detection of a SIMP or universality of the parameterization is implied.
variables: n_chi: physical dark particle number density
n_chi,eq: equilibrium number density at the common temperature
<sigma v^2>_3->2: thermally averaged 3-to-2 number-changing reaction coefficient
formulas.regime: Original effectively one-species SIMP thermal 3-to-2 paradigm with kinetic bath equilibrium; model-specific collision terms, chemical potentials and extra coupled species require changes.
formulas.units: In c=ℏ=k_B=1, n has E^3, H has E, <sigma v^2>_3->2 has E^-5 and <sigma v>_ann has E^-2; all terms have E^4.
formulas.theoryRelationship: Source-specific canonical collision-balance equation for a SIMP mechanism, not the mathematical definition of all strongly self-interacting dark matter.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1402.5143v2, printed p.4 / PDF page 4, Eq. (21), section 'Solving the Boltzmann equation'; visually checked the n^3−n^2 n_eq and n^2−n_eq^2 terms and both minus signs.

formulas.name: SIMP 3-to-2 thermal-rate parametrization
formulas.description: A dimensionally normalized definition of the effective 3-to-2 thermal rate used in the original SIMP freeze-out estimate.
assumptions: Single effective SIMP mass scale m_DM and dimensionless alpha_eff as defined by the original paper.
The parameter alpha_eff is not universally constant across temperature, model field content, nonperturbative enhancements or mediator masses.
Rate normalization is paper-specific; no standard 2-to-2 cross-section interpretation is valid for this 3-to-2 coefficient.
formulas.regime: One-mass-scale effective SIMP parametrization, not a derived cross section for arbitrary microscopic dark-sector models.
formulas.units: Natural units c=ℏ=k_B=1: [<sigma v^2>] = mass^-5, [m_DM] = mass and alpha_eff is dimensionless.
formulas.theoryRelationship: Defining effective-rate parametrization for the original single-species SIMP freeze-out estimate.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1402.5143v2, printed p.2 / PDF page 2, Eq. (6) immediately after 3-to-2 freeze-out condition Eq. (5); source explicitly describes alpha_eff as effective strength.

formulas.name: ELDER separately conserved dark-sector comoving entropy
formulas.plain: a^3 s'_chi ≃ a^3 m_chi n_chi / T' = constant
formulas.description: Approximate dark-sector comoving entropy during the cannibal epoch after elastic decoupling and before dark 3-to-2 freeze-out.
assumptions: Elastic scattering with visible matter has kinetically decoupled, while number-changing 3-to-2 interactions maintain chemical equilibrium within the nonrelativistic dark sector.
Separate comoving dark-sector entropy conservation in the specified epoch, not a general equality during visible-dark thermal contact or after chemical freeze-out.
The expression s'_chi ≈ m_chi n_chi/T' neglects subleading nonrelativistic thermodynamic terms.
variables: T': dark-sector temperature, different from visible-sector temperature T
formulas.regime: Nonrelativistic cannibalization between ELDER kinetic decoupling and 3-to-2 chemical freeze-out.
formulas.units: Entropy density s' is volume^-1; a^3 s' is comoving entropy (for a dimensionless scale factor). Set k_B=1 consistently.
formulas.theoryRelationship: Source-scoped thermodynamic approximation underlying the ELDER dark-sector temperature evolution.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1512.04545v1, printed p.2 / PDF page 2, Eq. (1), first displayed equality; the second proportionality in Eq. (1) depends on additional cosmological approximations.

formulas.name: ELDER approximate cannibal-epoch temperature
formulas.plain: T' ≃ T_d / [1 + (3 / x_d) ln(T_d / T)], x_d := m_chi / T_d
formulas.description: An approximate slower cooling law for a nonrelativistic ELDER dark gas after kinetic decoupling from the visible bath.
assumptions: ELDER thermal history after kinetic decoupling while 3-to-2 self-annihilations maintain dark chemical equilibrium.
Dark sector separately conserves comoving entropy; visible-sector entropy is treated as adiabatic with a proportional to T^-1 over the displayed interval.
T_d is the visible-sector temperature at elastic decoupling, and x_d=m_chi/T_d is positive; T below T_d in the epoch under discussion.
This approximate temperature history is not a universal decoupling bound or a detector prediction.
variables: T_d: plasma temperature when elastic scattering decouples
x_d: m_chi/T_d, dark-particle mass divided by decoupling temperature
formulas.regime: Approximate nonrelativistic 3-to-2 cannibal epoch of the original ELDER mechanism; not valid prior to elastic decoupling or after chemical freeze-out.
formulas.units: T', T and T_d are temperatures or energies in k_B=1 units; x_d and the logarithm argument are dimensionless.
formulas.theoryRelationship: Approximate model-dependent consequence of separately conserved dark-sector entropy in the original ELDER proposal.

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:1512.04545v1, printed p.2 / PDF page 2, Eq. (2) following entropy equation Eq. (1); visually inspected the plus sign and 3 x_d^-1 logarithm.

relations.note: SIMP 3-to-2 number-changing freeze-out can coexist with 2-to-2 self-scattering, but the mere existence of self-interactions does not establish the SIMP thermal relic mechanism.
relations.evidenceNote: Editorial conceptual intersection. Do not infer a sourced directed historical or equivalence claim.

relations.note: Both are thermal relic paradigms, but a WIMP one-species 2-to-2 annihilation history and an ELDER elastic-decoupling-controlled abundance describe different regimes.
relations.evidenceNote: Editorial conceptual overlap only; model-specific thermal history and pair annihilation differ.
